canonical_question: How is the theoretical saturation magnetization (Ms) in emu/g calculated for specific fcc and C14 phase compositions in FeCoNiTi high-entropy alloys, and what are the specific chemical formulas and molecular weights used in these derivations?

question_variants.question: What is the exact chemical composition of the fcc phase used for the entropy calculation (Fe 21.3 Co 24.8 Ni 32.2 Ti 21.6), and how was it derived from the multiphase alloy?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The exact chemical composition of the fcc phase is Fe 21.3 Co 24.8 Ni 32.2 Ti 21.6. It was derived from EDX analysis of the multiphase alloy, and the volume fraction was determined via XRD.

answers.answer: Chemical composition analysis indicates that the fcc phase is Fe 21.3 Co 24.8 Ni 32.2 Ti 21.6. This was determined by analyzing the parent alloy composed of fcc and C14 phases, and a specific alloy (Fe 27 Co 27 Ni 17 Ti 29) was synthesized to match the C14 phase composition for comparison.
answers.measurement_outcome: Composition of fcc phase identified as Fe 21.3 Co 24.8 Ni 32.2 Ti 21.6.
answers.mechanism: Chemical composition analysis indicates that the fcc phase is Fe 21.3 Co 24.8 Ni 32.2 Ti 21.6.
answers.boundary_limitation: None stated regarding the derivation method.
evidence_spans: As mentioned in the next section, the as-cast FeCoNiTi is composed of the fcc and hexagonal C14 phases with the volume ratio of V fcc : V C14 = 57:43.
Chemical composition analysis indicates that the fcc phase is Fe 21.3 Co 24.8 Ni 32.2 Ti 21.6 , while the C14 phase is Fe 27.3 Co 26.6 Ni 17.4 Ti 28.7 .

To determine which phase is responsible for each ordering, we prepared as-cast Fe 27 Co 27 Ni 17 Ti 29 , corresponding to Fe 27.3 Co 26.6 Ni 17.4 Ti 28.7 of the C14 phase in FeCoNiTi, using an analogous procedure.

source_evidence_spans: We comment here on the configurational entropy of the fcc phase (Fe 21.3 Co 24.8 Ni 32.2 Ti 21.6 ).
